Resolves #3589

Developers can create an editable workspace theme from a selected existing skin with `create-theme`. The generator preserves effective Engine/package/workspace files, retargets only theme-class selectors, and keeps Sass dependencies resolvable without overwriting existing themes or changing application config. The theming guide now explains the generated snapshot and file-level build precedence.

Evidence: L3 (real generator and theme-builder processes in disposable physical workspaces) → L3 required (usable generated source and compiled theme-map entries). No residuals; browser appearance is not claimed separately from compiled CSS parity.

## AC Evidence

No structured ACs on #3589; the ticket's intake acceptance record maps to:

| Consumer outcome | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Scaffold a theme from an existing base | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/createTheme.spec.mjs` exercises CLI flags, discovery, complete snapshots and Engine/package/workspace precedence. |
| Build the generated skin | CI-covered: the real builder emits Global/component CSS and theme-map membership; all shipped base entry sheets compile to matching CSS structure and values after selector retargeting. |
| Preserve existing files and dependencies | CI-covered: refusal snapshots, exact selector/asset boundaries, internal partials, shared imports and multi-URL Sass imports. |

## Deltas from ticket

Uses syntax-aware SCSS, selector and value parsers rather than text replacement, so URLs and literals retain their names. The parsers are development dependencies, following #5105; scaffolded workspaces install the Engine's build tools through create-app's postinstall. Both generation and compilation use that setup. Argument parsing and terminal prompts use Node built-ins. Generated values are an editable snapshot; shared imports continue to refer to their original owner. No new runtime inheritance layer.

Change class: capability (`feat`). Structural fast-path: `buildScripts/create/theme.mjs` follows the existing `create/app.mjs` and `create/scss.mjs` generator role; the spec follows `unit/buildScripts/createExample.spec.mjs`.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the repository's shared PR-baseline jobs provide the hosted body and substrate checks.

## Test Evidence

Outside-CI scaffolded-workspace check: the normal `npm pack` lifecycle produced the candidate tarball. A clean physical workspace declared that tarball as its Engine dependency and used create-app's postinstall command: `cd node_modules/neo.mjs && npm i && npm run bundle-parse5 && npm run bundle-marked`. After `npm install --include=dev`, its installed generator created `theme-installed` from `theme-neo-dark`, and its installed `themes.mjs -n -e dev -t theme-installed` built Global/component CSS and both theme maps. The Engine manifest has no runtime dependencies; all three parsers are devDependencies. The committed isolation case resolves their physical dependency graph from inside the installed Engine. This replaces the earlier production-only receipt, which did not establish a usable generation-and-build workflow.

## Post-Merge Validation

No deferred acceptance work. Publication follows the normal Engine release path.
